H2NY01190.name: Nick LaLota
H2NY01190.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 1st District since 2022; Navy veteran and former Amityville Village Trustee, Suffolk County elections commissioner, and legislative chief of staff.

positions.stance: Supports securing the border, deporting dangerous criminal illegal immigrants, and "practical immigration reforms" for those who have lived and worked peacefully in America.
Says he has "consistently backed the men and women who wear the badge" and opposes cashless bail and New York's ban on 287(g) agreements.
America "should have the strongest, most lethal military in the world," with military decisions based on merit and readiness, "not DEI mandates or political agendas."
"You earned it, and you should keep more of it"; cites quadrupling the SALT deduction cap to $40,000 and cutting taxes on overtime and tips.
Believes "every American deserves access to high-quality, affordable health care" and says he has worked with both parties to lower costs and expand access.

H6NY01159.name: Chris Gallant
H6NY01159.bio: Black Hawk pilot, air traffic controller, firefighter, and union leader.

positions.stance: Aims to "lower the cost of living so Long Island families can stay here," including permanent SALT relief and cracking down on price gouging.
Wants Long Island "prepared for the next storm" and to fix roads, bridges, water systems, and broadband.
Pledges to protect Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security, "lower prescription drug costs," and make health care more affordable and accessible.
Wants Long Island to be "a national model for veteran care" with faster access, stronger mental health services, and housing support.
Will "fight for the wages, protections, and opportunities that Long Island's working people have earned" and supports union pathways to the middle class.

H0NY02234.name: Andrew Garbarino
H0NY02234.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 2nd District since 2021 and Chairman of the House Homeland Security Committee; third-generation small business owner.

positions.stance: Has "fought to lower taxes, reduce unnecessary regulations," and cites raising the SALT deduction cap from $10,000 to $40,000.
Believes there is "a solemn obligation" to ensure veterans receive earned care and benefits, including mental health services and access at the Northport VA.
Opposes efforts to defund the police and introduced the POLICE Act making assault on first responders a deportable offense.
Says the federal government must "enforce our immigration laws, stop the flow of fentanyl," and give Border Patrol the resources it needs.
Supports "an all-of-the-above energy strategy" and has backed clean energy tax incentives and funding for Long Island water quality and coastal resiliency.

H6NY02140.name: Patrick Halpin
H6NY02140.bio: Former Suffolk County Executive and former Suffolk County Water Authority Chairman.

positions.stance: Will fight to make life more affordable by expanding housing for working families and "standing up to corporate price gouging and monopolies."
"Healthcare is a Right, Not a Privilege"; supports building toward universal Medicare coverage while protecting existing coverage and lowering drug prices.
Believes Long Island can create more housing "without sacrificing the character of our neighborhoods," building where it makes sense.
Will fight to "make polluters pay, protect clean water and clean air, strengthen climate resilience" and safeguard Long Island's aquifer.
Refuses corporate PAC money, supports banning congressional stock trading, and wants to end pay-to-play politics and strengthen ethics laws.

H6NY03247.name: Tom Suozzi
H6NY03247.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 3rd District; attorney and CPA, former Mayor of Glen Cove and former Nassau County Executive.

positions.stance: Wants to "get rid of irresponsible tariffs that are driving up prices" and fight for trade deals that bring manufacturing jobs back.
Calls for phasing out the Iran war, "smart diplomacy," modern defense spending, and limits on a president's use of the military without congressional authorization.
Wants to "rein in federal spending" and enact a bipartisan fiscal framework to reduce the deficit and lower interest-rate pressure.
Supports cutting red tape to build energy projects faster, including "clean energy, natural gas, nuclear, transmission, and storage."
Wants to protect the tax credits that lower insurance premiums, invest in prevention and primary care, and make long-term care more affordable.

H0NY02267.name: Mike LiPetri
H0NY02267.bio: Attorney and former New York State Assemblyman.

positions.stance: "Affordability starts with letting Americans keep more of what they earn"; supports lifting the SALT cap and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
Says officers and their families "deserve and have earned our full and unapologetic support."
"We are a nation of laws"; supports continuing to deport criminals here illegally and requiring every immigrant to enter legally.
Says any attempt to boycott, divest from, or sanction Israel "must be shut down" and that antisemitism "cannot be tolerated."
Supports a system emphasizing "personal, portable, and preventative care," letting Americans choose their doctors and keep coverage across jobs or states.
Will keep "fighting to lower the tax burden by restoring the full State and Local Tax (SALT) Deduction" and seeking more relief for Nassau families and seniors.
Says she will "support law enforcement" in Congress.
Will work to "ensure the southern border can never be opened again."

H2NY04244.name: Laura Gillen
H2NY04244.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 4th District since 2025; lawyer and former Hempstead Town Supervisor.

H8NY06048.name: Gregory Meeks
H8NY06048.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 5th District in his fourteenth term; lead Democrat and former Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

H6NY05127.name: George Marsh
H6NY05127.bio: Former employee of the New York City Mayor's Office.

positions.stance: Wants to "modernize our roads, bridges and water systems" and says he will re-introduce the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act on day one.
Supports investing in "reliable public transit, safer streets, and modern transportation."
Would "cut red tape, expand access to capital," and make it easier for neighborhood businesses to start, grow, and hire.
Wants to "secure federal investment for projects that strengthen communities" and improve public spaces.
Wants to "lower everyday costs, strengthen economic opportunity, and ensure working families can build a secure future."

H2NY06116.name: Grace Meng
H2NY06116.bio: Member of Congress from Queens and member of the House Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: Defends "a woman's constitutional right to make decisions about her own body" and access to reproductive care from abortion to contraception to IVF.
"She will continue to oppose any and all efforts to undermine Social Security and Medicare."
Supports small businesses, a $15 minimum wage, and making it "easier to join a union and collectively bargain."
A founding member of the Medicare for All Congressional Caucus who supports expanding Medicare so every American has comprehensive health coverage.
Fighting "to safeguard Medicare and Social Security" and to combat scams that target seniors.

H4NY06047.name: Joseph Chou
H4NY06047.bio: Queens small business owner and naturalized citizen.

positions.stance: Pledges "a balanced tax policy that fosters growth and lightens burdens," particularly for working families and new small businesses, plus fair student loan interest rates.
Advocates provisions that "empower parents to make informed decisions regarding their children's education and health," plus healthcare access and affordable childcare.
Supports "robust options for public, private, and alternative learning pathways" and curricula including vocational training, the arts, and the sciences.
Supports "safe and secure borders alongside a compassionate approach to immigration" and more inter-agency cooperation on significant criminal threats.
Committed to evaluating and reforming the cashless bail system "in a way that balances justice with mercy."

H6NY07271.name: Melvin Rivera
H6NY07271.bio: Community activist, tenant organizer, and advocate for working families in Brooklyn for more than 30 years.

positions.stance: Wants to "transform public assistance into a system that builds independence—not dependency," restoring apprenticeship programs tied to high-income industries.
Backs a Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act giving tenants first right to offer on sale, plus an "Anti-Flip Tax to stop predatory speculation."
Wants an economy "that works for workers, not monopolies," with more micro-loans and startup capital and fewer unnecessary small business regulations.
Wants to expand trade schools, apprenticeships, and industrial high schools and "return more control to parents and communities."
Calls to "repeal the Taylor Law" and protect workers' right to organize, protest, and negotiate fair wages.

H6NY07214.name: Claire Valdez
H6NY07214.bio: New York Assemblymember and former union organizer.

positions.stance: Will fight to "strengthen and pass the PRO Act, establish active federal support for union organizing, and end 'at will' employment."
Will fight for "universal rent control," public investment in housing supply, and tenant power with landlord accountability.
Will "sponsor Medicare for All on Day One"; says "Health care is a human right."
Will fight to "dismantle and abolish ICE" and push for immigration reform that legalizes the status of millions of immigrants.
Wants a foreign policy centered on human rights and peace, and to "end all weapons sales and military aid to Israel."

H2NY10092.name: Hakeem Jeffries
H2NY10092.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 8th District since 2013 and House Democratic Leader since 2023.

positions.stance: Working to lower child care, health care, education, and prescription drug costs, and to "expand the Child Tax Credit" for working families.
Supports "universal background checks for firearm purchases and a ban on assault weapons" and strengthening police-community relationships.
Believes that if you work hard and play by the rules, you should be able to buy a home, educate your children, and "retire with grace and dignity."
Pushing for "a bold investment in our nation's public housing infrastructure" and homes existing residents can afford.
Supports enshrining Roe v. Wade protections in federal law; believes women, families, and doctors should make decisions about pregnancy.

H4NY11138.name: Yvette Clarke
H4NY11138.bio: Member of Congress representing Brooklyn's 9th District and Co-Chair of the Caribbean Caucus.

positions.stance: Advocates keeping Brooklyn "affordable for everyday residents," reformulating HUD's area median income, and reinvesting in public housing.
Says "we are a nation of immigrants"; supports protecting DACA and TPS recipients and "is a proponent for the abolishment of ICE."
Says affordable, adequate healthcare "should be a right for all Americans - not a privilege"; supports Medicare for All.
A "strong advocate for critical services that support women's reproductive rights" and a proponent of paid family leave.
"A strong supporter of LGBTQ+ rights" who backs the Equality Act prohibiting discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity.

H6NY09145.name: Joel Anabilah-Azumah
H6NY09145.bio: Brooklyn small businessman and Brooklyn College men's volleyball coach, with a civil engineering degree.

positions.stance: Says the U.S. should bring manufacturing home and "do our best to stay out of a major war so that reinvestment in American infrastructure can take place."
Raises concern that AI "has the potential to evade human guard rails" and asks how to keep government accountable as AI operates it.
Says "the federal minimum wage has to increase from $7.25/hour to $17/hour" as part of reducing the size of the welfare state.
Calls for "a major infrastructure campaign to rebuild roads, rail, pipelines, and new nuclear power plants."
Pledges to "be the political champion for the Utica Avenue Subway," a full-length subway from Eastern Parkway to Kings Plaza.

H6NY10176.name: Brad Lander
H6NY10176.bio: Former New York City Comptroller and former New York City Councilmember.

positions.stance: Has "called for abolishing ICE since 2018" and supports reforming the immigration system.
Will "investigate lawless Trump officials" and work to ensure "that Presidents are not above the law."
Rejects corporate PAC money, will vote to overturn Citizens United, and supports a stock trading ban for Members of Congress.
Says Congress should expand the Supreme Court "to 13 justices" and advance term limits or staggered appointments.
Has worked "to build and preserve affordable housing for his entire career" and proposes social bonds to finance social housing.

H6NY10218.name: Jennifer Moore
H6NY10218.bio: Lifelong Brooklynite and Republican operative; Republican and Conservative Party nominee for New York's 10th District.

positions.stance: "Support the NYPD and first responders"; rejects soft-on-crime approaches.
"Fight the cost-of-living crisis"; says New Yorkers are being priced out and need "practical solutions, not more ideology."
"Reject radical agendas that divide our city" and stand for working families, parents, and small business owners.
Says the district deserves "a representative who listens to all residents — not just the loudest activists."

H0NY11078.name: Nicole Malliotakis
H0NY11078.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 11th District since 2021 and member of the House Ways and Means Committee; former five-term New York State Assemblywoman.

positions.stance: Wrote Goldie's Act requiring the USDA "to crack down on abusive practices by commercial dog breeders and confiscate suffering animals."
"A strong proponent of educational freedom and student safety"; supports a trained police officer in every school and expanding parental school choice.
Believes reforms should "make it easier to vote and harder to cheat," including voter identification and regular maintenance of voter rolls.
Used her seat on the House Select Committee on the Coronavirus Crisis "to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci and NIH staff accountable" for their pandemic actions.
Describes herself as "a leader in environmental protection" and cites securing funds to complete the East Shore Sea Wall.

H6NY11265.name: Michael DeCillis
H6NY11265.bio: Former police officer and teacher and third-generation union member with 35 years in public service.

positions.stance: Says "Congress needs to be a co-equal branch of government" and should enact new reforms restricting presidential power.
"We need to reduce the tax burden on the working class and the billionaires need to pay their fair share."
Will "stop the dismantling of the Department of Education" and believes more investment is needed in public education.
Does not take money from corporate PACs "or any PACs that lobby on behalf of a single foreign nation."
Believes "climate change is real" and supports penalties for polluters and investment in sewer, drainage, and shoreline protection.

H6NY12172.name: Micah Lasher
H6NY12172.bio: New York State Assemblymember who previously held senior government posts, including in the New York Attorney General's Office.

positions.stance: Will "use every procedural tool in our arsenal" to block the Republican agenda and, if Democrats regain the House, pursue aggressive oversight hearings.
Will "massively expand federal investment in child care," expand housing tax credits and rental assistance, and raise and index the minimum wage.
Will "fight to abolish ICE" and support the For the People Act and John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
Believes "health care should be a right, not a privilege"; will push to pass Medicare for All or a similar universal plan.
Supports universal background checks, reinstating the assault weapons ban, a national Red Flag law, and more investment in mental healthcare.

H6NY12404.name: Caroline Shinkle
H6NY12404.bio: Harvard Law School and MIT graduate with a background in corporate law and international central banking.

positions.stance: "Protect the Paycheck" by reducing federal income tax on W-2 wages, increasing housing supply, and balancing the federal budget.
Supports making student loan interest "fully tax deductible, with no income caps," school choice, curriculum transparency, and trades and STEM training.
Will "champion, support, and empower our law enforcement officers" and end policies that return violent offenders to the streets.
Will prosecute sources of funds supporting antisemitic violence and "unapologetically stand with the Jewish community of New York City and our ally Israel."
Wants to "reintroduce competition into the healthcare marketplace and enhance price transparency" and root out insurance fraud.

H6NY13279.name: Darializa Avila Chevalier
H6NY13279.bio: Investigator at a Harlem public defenders office, CUNY PhD student, and college instructor.

positions.stance: Will sign onto bills "to secure housing as a human right, universal healthcare, union protections, a $15 minimum wage and more."
Will "fight to abolish the deportation machine, expand pathways to citizenship, secure free legal representation for immigrants."
Wants to divest taxpayer dollars spent on "senseless wars abroad" and invest them in child tax credits and baby bonds.
Will "fight to protect all tenants, fully fund Section 8, fully fund NYCHA, prevent deed theft, and build affordable housing."
Supports Medicare for All, "a free, universal system" covering primary, mental, dental, vision, hearing, reproductive, and long-term care.

H6NY13303.name: Jomo Williams
H6NY13303.bio: U.S. Army veteran, Harlem business owner, paralegal, and former Verizon communications technician.

positions.stance: Supports "Universal Capitalism (Direct Wealth Creation & Capital Access for Working Families)" rather than socialism.
Says "No to Defund Police"; supports fully funding public safety and a complete criminal justice system overhaul.
Fights for "Universal Attorney Access in all civil matters to protect civil rights," building on Right to Counsel in housing courts.
Supports closing and securing borders, pausing immigration to protect local wages and housing, and backing the bipartisan Dignity Act with his proposed addendums.
Supports enforcing U.S. borders, Puerto Rico statehood, Dominican Republic sovereignty, and a "Two-State Solution for peaceful coexistence."

H8NY15148.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
H8NY15148.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 14th District since 2019.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All to "guarantee healthcare for all people, curb costs, and improve long-term health."
"Housing As a Human Right": protect current occupants, repair public housing, and build new affordable housing.
"Stop investing in the business of wars; invest in peace and diplomacy."
Wants to "rebuild the unions, invest in people not corporations," and create a federal jobs guarantee.
"Instead of investing in mass incarceration, we need to invest in the most vulnerable members of our society."

H6NY14251.name: Diamant Hysenaj
H6NY14251.bio: Construction small business owner and entrepreneur who immigrated to New York at age nine.

positions.stance: Calls for "Affordable Rent. Quality Homes," citing his experience as a small business owner in construction.
Wants "a system that's tough but fair: secure borders, faster citizenship for the law-abiding, and real support for our neighborhoods."
"Support our small businesses and create jobs so everyone can have a good life."
Wants to lower healthcare costs and "get rid of waste and fraud, giving back to the people, not the insurance companies."
Supports "safe streets" so "kids can play outside again."

H0NY15160.name: Ritchie Torres
H0NY15160.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 15th District and former New York City Councilmember.
